plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated hill workout to build climbing strength and trail-specific power.
Higher overall training volume (166 minutes vs 249 minutes) allows for greater physiological adaptation, assuming the athlete can handle it.
More rest days (4 vs 1) which is beneficial for recovery and injury prevention, especially when incorporating hill work.
plan_b_advantages: Potentially lower risk of overtraining due to the lower volume.
The longer runs on days 6 and 7 provide some exposure to longer distances, which could be beneficial for endurance.
reasoning: Given the goal of becoming a faster trail runner, Plan A appears to be the better choice. While both plans focus on aerobic development, Plan A incorporates a dedicated hill workout, which is crucial for trail running performance. Plan B relies solely on easy runs, which, while important for base building, won't effectively develop the strength and power needed for climbing and descending trails. The higher volume in Plan A, while requiring more commitment, is likely to yield greater improvements in overall fitness and speed.
